brief: 5 red flags in your first 10 hires that will haunt you for 3 years.

slots.body: One toxic early hire can poison culture, stall momentum, and cost you three years of growth.
Early employees write the playbook everyone else follows. Get it wrong, and the debt compounds daily.
slots.quote: Culture is simply the worst behavior a founder is willing to tolerate.

slots.body: Hiring for vibe instead of velocity creates clubs, not companies. Competence is what scales; chemistry is a bonus.
slots.quote: A nice person who can't execute is still a bad hire.

slots.body: If a candidate ghosts you before day one, they will disappear when deadlines hit. Responsiveness is a proxy for urgency.
slots.quote: How they chase the job is how they'll chase the work.

slots.body: Candidates who ask zero hard questions about the business aren't hungry. They're looking for a paycheck, not a mission.
slots.quote: The best hires interview you harder than you interview them.

slots.body: Desperation makes founders pitch candidates instead of probing them. The best talent wants to be screened, not sold.
slots.quote: If you're begging, you're already losing.

slots.body: Founders often build teams that mirror their strengths. That leaves fatal gaps in judgment, skill, and perspective.
slots.quote: You don't need more you. You need more better.

slots.body: Share this with your cofounder and audit your last three offers. Prevention is cheaper than replacement.
